attachments.origin_landmark: upper border of the cricoid arch, laterally (the laryngeal cartilages are not modeled as skeletal elements in this pass -- approximated via the adjacent hyoid attachment region)
attachments.insertion_landmark: muscular process of the arytenoid cartilage

innervation.note: Corrected: this LEFT muscle had cited the RIGHT recurrent laryngeal nerve, the mirror of the error found earlier in the nerve tree, where the left branch had listed the right muscles.

actions: adducts the vocal folds, closing the rima glottidis

functional_compartments.name: Single fiber population
functional_compartments.function_note: The principal adductor, and the direct antagonist of posterior cricoarytenoid.
functional_compartments.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

motor_endplate_zones.reference_line_to: upper border of the cricoid arch, laterally (origin)
motor_endplate_zones.notes: Unlike posterior cricoarytenoid, LCA showed a single homogeneous nerve plexus confined to the middle third of the muscle in all 5 specimens studied, consistent with a single neuromuscular compartment (no evidence for functionally distinct medial/lateral zones despite some investigators' suggestion that its lateral edge assists abduction). The zone given here is that middle third.
motor_endplate_zones.source: Sanders I, Mu L, Wu BL, Biller HF, 'The intramuscular nerve supply of the human lateral cricoarytenoid muscle', Acta Otolaryngol 113(5):679-682 (1993), doi:10.3109/00016489309135884 (https://doi.org/10.3109/00016489309135884) -- 5 human larynges, Sihler staining -- retrieved via PubMed

source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

ultrasound_injection_approach.transducer_placement: Percutaneous EMG-guided injection through the cricothyroid membrane, not ultrasound: using the same membrane-puncture approach as for thyroarytenoid, the needle is directed slightly more inferolaterally and deeper to reach LCA, which lies just deep/inferior to thyroarytenoid between the arytenoid's muscular process and the lateral cricoid arch.
ultrasound_injection_approach.depth_layer: Deep to thyroarytenoid, in the paraglottic space between the cricoid arch and the arytenoid muscular process.
ultrasound_injection_approach.identification_cues: EMG activity increasing with phonation/adduction, as for thyroarytenoid; the two muscles are not reliably distinguished by surface landmarks, so operators rely on needle depth and angle rather than a distinct EMG signature.
structures_at_risk: thyroarytenoid, immediately superficial -- in practice the two are frequently co-injected/co-diffused rather than separately targeted (aniline-blue tracer reaches LCA in over 90% of thyroarytenoid injections)
cricoid cartilage, deep to the muscle -- limits how far medially/deep the needle should be advanced
airway lumen, if the needle is advanced through the full thickness of the paraglottic tissues
ultrasound_injection_approach.notes: LCA is rarely injected as an isolated target; it is most often treated as part of the thyroarytenoid injection for adductor spasmodic dysphonia (by direct spread) or, less commonly, deliberately co-injected with thyroarytenoid for a stronger adductor effect. Guidance is by EMG, never ultrasound.
ultrasound_injection_approach.source: Blitzer A, Brin MF, Stewart CF, 'Botulinum toxin management of spasmodic dysphonia (laryngeal dystonia): a 12-year experience in more than 900 patients', Laryngoscope 108(10):1435-1441 (1998), doi:10.1097/00005537-199810000-00003 (https://doi.org/10.1097/00005537-199810000-00003); Alonso VM, Chagury AA, Hachiya A, Imamura R, Tsuji DH, Sennes LU, 'Diffusion of aniline blue injected into the thyroarytenoid muscle as a proxy for botulinum toxin injection...', Int Arch Otorhinolaryngol 17(3):315-320 (2013), doi:10.7162/S1809-977720130003000012 (https://doi.org/10.7162/S1809-977720130003000012) -- 94.3% of specimens showed diffusion from thyroarytenoid into LCA -- both retrieved via PubMed
